title: 4...bxc6, the other recapture
intro:
Black recaptures towards the edge. It keeps a pawn on d7 and a route for the knight to e7 and g6, and it leaves the queenside pawns in a heap: a6, c6 and c7 with nothing on b7.

## Why this is good news

The doubled pawns are worse here than in the main line, because Black has three pawn islands from move four and the c-pawns can never advance without help. What Black gets in return is the half-open b-file and a bishop that can come to a6 or b7. It is playable and it is a concession, and the engine agrees: this is the one line in the course where White is close to half a pawn better straight out of the opening.

## Your answer

Look at g7 as well, once the knight goes to g6: in the main line of this chapter it is a free pawn, because the rook on h8 has never defended it.

5.d4 at once. Black's e-pawn has nothing but the queen behind it, so the centre opens on White's terms, and the queen recapture on d4 is safe here because Black has no knight on c6 to gain time against her. Then Nc3, Be3, castle long, and play down the file at the pawns that cannot defend themselves.

## Typical mistakes at this level

Playing the quiet 5.O-O out of habit, which is sound and lets Black free the position with ...d5. Recapturing on d4 with the knight, which offers Black exactly the trade that helps him. Castling short, away from the side where Black is weak. And forgetting which pawn is the target: it is c6 and c7, not a6.
